feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant platform/strategy depth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing scope from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility and leadership narrative.  
- Strong alignment between headline, summary, and experience: digital strategy, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, and cross-channel communications are consistently reinforced.  
- Writing is polished and specific, with good use of concrete platforms and scale indicators like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond scope metrics: include performance gains, engagement improvements, efficiency wins, revenue/support outcomes, or campaign impact to increase impact.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap heavily and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience”; standardize comma usage in lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); and consider changing “French (A2/Learning)” to “French (A2, learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more specific value proposition, tighter phrasing, and less overlap with the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Lead with seniority and sector relevance: emphasize digital strategy leadership for mission-driven, advocacy, or membership organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a more outcome-oriented summary focused on cross-channel strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, web and platform modernization, editorial operations, and the systems that enable coordinated, organization-wide communications. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” repeat heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid adding tools/platform names here; those are already covered well elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening wording and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, senior-level phrasing: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Editorial operations & governance • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS management • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder alignment & cross-functional collaboration • Advocacy, policy & member communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Change “Multi-channel communication” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” for stronger grammar and scope.
- Replace “Web & CMS administration” with “Web platform & CMS management” to sound more strategic and less junior.
- Consider ordering by relevance to recent roles: strategy, web/platforms, editorial operations, analytics, stakeholder leadership, advocacy, multimedia.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, cross-channel communications, analytics, and multimedia.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design”; combine to avoid redundancy.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and Recent Projects. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into impact-focused lines, e.g.:
- “Built Drupal campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved enterprise web operations by streamlining CMS workflows, front-end implementation, troubleshooting, and cross-team publishing practices.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Add measurable detail where possible: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search accuracy/engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics there.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the header/Core Competencies; use one concise bullet, not several.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact role with good scale metrics; it should read more like an executive achievement entry and less like a responsibility list. Tighten the lead, foreground the website modernization and analytics work, and add outcome language where possible.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening summary with an achievement-led line: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a national association serving county officials.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact phrasing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video content.”
- Add measurable results if available for analytics/governance work: reporting speed, stakeholder adoption, publishing efficiency, traffic/email growth, or cost savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Video-program growth overlaps with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on building the studio/capacity, not recurring video production.
- “Governance/publishing workflows” also appears elsewhere; here, frame it as enterprise-scale operational improvement.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to executional leadership and channel growth, with sharper verbs and any available metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope without repeating the Director role: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Owned production and distribution of four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable/process outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved workflows” and “strengthened editorial coordination” are too close to the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/freelance experience. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level leadership and governance rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit
- Replace with more distinctive, senior phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems, and workflow design
- Cross-channel communications operations and team leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy
- Audience-centered planning for complex information environments
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “content strategy” or “communications operations” to better match the CV’s platform/governance focus.
- If space allows, add one sharper qualifier such as “high-volume” or “multi-stakeholder” to reflect the scale shown in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” already appear almost verbatim in the header/Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeats language covered in multiple NACo roles; avoid stacking similar phrasing across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent work—especially Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from platform list to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop or de-emphasize older/less central platforms unless they are job-target relevant; keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if required by the role.
- Remove “jQuery” from this topline section; it feels dated and is better left in Technical + IT if needed.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “supporting large public-facing sites and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Technical + IT” section almost verbatim; Topline Skills should stay higher-level.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and decision-making impact over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization” rather than only naming products.
- Tighten to 5–7 items and group tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio & Power BI” instead of listing each separately.
- Elevate business impact language: “KPI framework development,” “executive/leadership reporting,” “user behavior analysis,” “SEO & performance optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy & KPI design - Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio & Power BI - User behavior insights with Microsoft Clarity - SEO, content performance & conversion analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid overemphasizing tools already proven in the 2022–2024 NACo role unless this section adds strategic scope.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented, emphasizing operational leadership rather than listing production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Live Event Delivery”
- Replace with tighter, higher-level bullets:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream, hybrid and virtual event delivery
- In-house studio buildout and operations
- PTZ camera and multi-camera production workflows
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. “Built and operated NACo’s first in-house video studio supporting advocacy programming and event coverage.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” already appear in Core Competencies; use this section to add specificity instead of repeating broad labels.
- Tool-level detail like editing software is already covered under “Multimedia & Creative Tools,” so avoid repeating software names here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this line to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than just listing names.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by strongest/recent platform: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/context instead of a pure list: “CMS platforms: Drupal (primary), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it reads lighter than the rest.
- If you want more impact, tie to scale in adjacent experience bullets rather than here; this section should stay concise.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This is nearly duplicated by Topline Skills [2], which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Avoid repeating “CMS modernization” here if it remains in Topline Skills; keep one section platform-focused and the other capability-focused.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and the more current tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop versioning (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used elsewhere consistently; it adds little value.
- Consider replacing “jQuery” with “JavaScript/jQuery” only if still actively used in recent Drupal work; otherwise remove to avoid dating the profile.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “used GTM and API integrations to support analytics and campaign functionality.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may also overlap with GitHub Actions; keep one section broader and this one tool-specific.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as an undifferentiated software list. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should emphasize systems you actually built or led, not every collaboration app used.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to: “Workflow Automation & Project Systems”
- Prioritize true automation/build tools first, then project platforms: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana”
- Move general collaboration tools out unless strategically important: remove “Slack • Teams” and likely “Basecamp • Trello” unless used to run major cross-team operations
- If space allows, add light context instead of a pure list: “Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana — used for editorial planning, approvals, intake, and cross-team workflow coordination”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Slack/Teams overlap more with collaboration than technical workflow systems, weakening this section’s focus

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this line should stay concise and tool-focused rather than restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS match: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Newsletter and campaign automation
- Keep ordering by strongest/recently used platform first; if Dynamics was less central than Higher Logic at NACo, list Higher Logic first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or “campaign management” here if those points are already covered in the NACo experience bullets.
- “Engagement Systems” is slightly vague; don’t broaden into CRM/automation language unless supported elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it clearly foundational/early-career, with sharper scope and any measurable outputs you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize build-stage impact: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Split the second sentence into concrete contributions: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and recurring video content; and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics if possible: number of livestreams, cadence of video updates, audience reach, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten management phrasing: use “mentored a digital media associate” or “provided day-to-day supervision to one associate” only if accurate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/early production rather than expansion.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this lighter and more execution-focused.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize concrete ownership and avoid overlapping too much with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and policy research projects for NACo programs while supporting digital content and multimedia initiatives.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to” with stronger verbs only where accurate: supported, produced, coordinated, launched.
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of research/program initiatives.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid claiming broad digital leadership here, since that growth is already shown in 2015–2024 roles.
